title: Wonder — constructed example sentences
description: One deliberately constructed candidate demonstration per canonical cell. These are illustrative examples selected for discussion, not part of the canon or verified sentence classifications.

examples.10: Behind the ivy-covered wall, they discovered the entrance to a forgotten garden.
examples.11: One brass key opened the passage from which every room in the old tower could be reached.
examples.12: When the jammed gate finally lifted, the ambulance could drive through.
examples.13: The new harbour chart showed three different routes to the island.
examples.14: With stepping stones across every stream, the children could reach cottages throughout the valley.
examples.15: A chain of footbridges now lets walkers cross the entire marsh without setting foot in the water.
examples.16: With the curfew lifted, the midnight train was an option again.
examples.17: The heated tunnel kept the mountain crossing open through winters that had once closed it.
examples.18: The miners broke through the wall that had stopped them for years and drove the tunnel into the mountain beyond.
examples.19: The fingerprint on the window belonged to the missing violinist.
examples.20: Against the silence of the cathedral, a single whispered word sounded immense.
examples.21: She called across the dark lake, and a lantern flashed once in answer.
examples.22: The ferry connects with the mountain train, which meets the last bus to the village.
examples.23: The farther the tide withdrew, the more of the wreck emerged.
examples.24: As the room cooled, the thermostat started the heater, whose warmth eventually made the thermostat switch it off.
examples.25: The arrangement of moons around the planet matched the arrangement of pebbles in the child's model, despite the enormous difference in scale.
examples.26: In the children's play, a wooden spoon served as the king's sceptre.
examples.27: One person began clapping, each neighbour caught the rhythm, and soon the whole hall was applauding together.
examples.28: The clock was seven minutes fast, so she reset its hands to the correct time.
examples.29: He tightened the violin string until its note matched the piano's A.
examples.30: With the broken fuse replaced, the lighthouse lamp shone again.
examples.31: She corrected the tide table until its predictions agreed with the observations at every harbour.
examples.32: By adjusting both hinges against the frame, the carpenter made the crooked doors meet perfectly.
examples.33: The pilot corrected the drift at each waypoint until the aircraft could follow its intended approach.
examples.34: The survey established that the ridge, not the river marked on every old map, was the true boundary.
examples.35: The plants recovered when she abandoned her rule of watering every morning and watered only when the soil needed it.
examples.36: Once the leak was repaired, the pump ran normally without the buckets, alarms and nightly emergency checks.
examples.37: Around the central hearth, the scattered stones became an oven, each finding its place in the structure.
examples.38: The loose pages became one book when they were sewn onto a common spine.
examples.39: With the conductor at the podium, the separate sections of the orchestra could perform as one.
examples.40: In the completed garden plan, every tree, path, bed and watercourse occupied its appointed place.
examples.41: The stone arch stood because every block pressed against its neighbours, each helping to hold the others in place.
examples.42: At the first downbeat, the strings, winds and percussion joined in a performance none could produce alone.
examples.43: When the dividing wall came down, the two courtyards became a single garden.
examples.44: After generations of separation, the two villages formed one community through their shared care of the only well.
examples.45: The five rescue crews abandoned their separate plans and carried out one coordinated rescue.
examples.46: After hearing both proposals, the council chose the stone bridge.
examples.47: The dispute was settled by their agreement to share the well on alternate days.
examples.48: At the last crossroads, the guide pointed left, ending their uncertainty about which way to go.
examples.49: When the missing ledger arrived, every unexplained entry in the three years of accounts could finally be reconciled.
examples.50: The inheritance was settled for every claimant under the terms they had all signed.
examples.51: With evacuation instructions agreed for every ward, the hospital could carry out the entire operation without another decision at each doorway.
examples.52: The verdict stood, and the few unanswered questions no longer required another hearing.
examples.53: The missing letter explained his silence that summer, and she no longer needed to ask why he had vanished.
examples.54: With the final obligation discharged, the ship could sail without waiting for another signature.
examples.01: That bright point above the chimney is Venus.
examples.02: Among the identical white envelopes, the one with the blue corner is hers.
examples.03: Any runner whose foot crosses the red line is immediately disqualified.
examples.04: The island's coastline divides naturally into cliffs, beaches, marshes and sheltered coves.
examples.05: In a choir of deep voices, her ordinarily low note was the highest in the room.
examples.06: The sorting machine now sends glass, paper and metal into three different chutes.
examples.07: Once thought to be a single species, the two birds are now recognised as distinct.
examples.08: Instead of measuring every singer against an ideal voice, she arranged the voices from lowest to highest.
examples.09: Once the blanket label of 'safe' was discarded, the inspector rejected the cracked beams and approved the sound ones.
